days.title: Arriving in Portugal
days.objective: You will greet, thank and excuse yourself, which is most of what the first hour in Portugal asks of you.
days.paretoFocus: Three courtesy words carry a visitor further than any amount of grammar: Portuguese people switch to English readily, and the way to keep them in Portuguese is to open in it.
drills: Say the right greeting for the time it is right now, out loud.
Say obrigado or obrigada according to YOUR own gender, five times.
Walk through it: greet, ask for help, thank them, say goodbye.

items: Which greeting do you use at 21:00?
What is the difference between com licença and desculpe?
How do you ask whether someone speaks English?

activities.title: Your first words
activities.intro: Whole phrases, not word lists. Say each one out loud before moving to the next.

items.en: Good morning. Do you speak English?
items.note: Asking this IN Portuguese is what earns you a patient answer.

items.en: Good afternoon. Can you help me?
Thank you very much for the help.
items.note: A woman says muito obrigada. The word agrees with whoever is speaking.

items.en: Please.
items.note: Heard far more than por favor in Portugal, and often written s.f.f.

items.en: Sorry, I do not speak Portuguese.
Excuse me, coming through.
items.note: For squeezing past somebody. Desculpe is for apologising.

items.en: Good evening. See you tomorrow.
items.note: Boa noite is both hello and goodbye once it is dark.

items.en: Goodbye and thank you.

activities.title: Choosing the right word
activities.intro: One courtesy word fits each situation better than the others.

questions.prompt: You need to get past somebody blocking a narrow aisle. You say:
questions.explanation: Com licença asks for room. Desculpe apologises for something you did.

questions.prompt: It is 21:00 and you walk into a restaurant. You greet them with:
questions.explanation: Once it is dark the greeting is boa noite, arriving as well as leaving.

questions.prompt: A woman wants to say thank you very much. She says:
questions.explanation: The word agrees with the speaker, so a woman says obrigada whoever she thanks.

questions.prompt: Which is the more Portuguese way to say please?
questions.explanation: Both are correct, but se faz favor is what you will hear in Portugal.

activities.title: In the street
activities.intro: You stop somebody to ask for help. Read both parts aloud, then only the Me lines.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Desculpe, fala inglês?
lines.en: Excuse me, do you speak English?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Um pouco. Diga.
lines.en: A little. Go ahead.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Bom dia. Pode ajudar-me?
lines.en: Good morning. Can you help me?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Com certeza. O que precisa?
lines.en: Of course. What do you need?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Desculpe, não falo português.
lines.en: Sorry, I do not speak Portuguese.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Não faz mal. Eu ajudo.
lines.en: No problem. I will help.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Muito obrigado pela ajuda.
lines.en: Thank you very much for the help.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: De nada. Boa tarde!
lines.en: You are welcome. Good afternoon!

days.title: A coffee, please
days.objective: You will order in a Portuguese café and pay, which is the transaction you will repeat most often.
days.paretoFocus: Coffee is the centre of Portuguese daily life and the café is the friendliest place to make your first mistakes. The whole exchange is four short phrases.
drills: Order your own real breakfast out loud, in Portuguese, before you drink it.
Say the four café phrases without looking: order, take away, bill, thanks.
Swap the pastry for something else and order that instead.

items: How do you ask for the bill?
What arrives if you order um café?
How do you say you want it to take away?

activities.title: At the counter
activities.intro: Order at the counter. Notice how short the Portuguese is compared with the English.

items.en: Excuse me, an espresso.
items.note: Faz favor alone works both as please and as a way to catch the eye. In Portugal um café IS an espresso.

items.hr: Um pastel de nata, se faz favor.
items.en: One custard tart, please.
A still water.
items.note: Com gás is sparkling. The waiter will ask which you want.

items.en: A large white coffee in a cup.
To take away, please.
Could you bring the bill?
How much is it?
It is excellent, thank you.

activities.title: In the cafe
activities.intro: Pick the phrase that gets you what you want.

questions.prompt: You want your coffee to go. You say:
questions.explanation: Para levar is takeaway. The opposite is para aqui.

questions.prompt: You ask for um café in Lisbon. You get:
questions.explanation: Um café means an espresso. For milk, ask for uma meia de leite.

questions.prompt: You are ready to pay. You say:
questions.explanation: A conta is the bill. Quanto é? also works at a counter.

questions.prompt: You want water without bubbles. You ask for:
questions.explanation: Sem gás is still, com gás is sparkling.

activities.title: Breakfast
activities.intro: Breakfast at a counter in Porto. Read it twice, the second time only as Me.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Bom dia! Diga lá.
lines.en: Good morning! Tell me.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Bom dia. Faz favor, um café.
lines.en: Good morning. Excuse me, an espresso.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Mais alguma coisa?
lines.en: Anything else?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Um pastel de nata, se faz favor.
lines.en: One custard tart, please.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: É para aqui ou para levar?
lines.en: Is it to have here or to take away?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Para levar, se faz favor.
lines.en: To take away, please.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: São dois euros e trinta.
lines.en: That is two euros thirty.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Quanto é? Ah, obrigado.
lines.en: How much is it? Ah, thank you.

days.title: How much does it cost?
days.objective: You will ask a price, say how you want to pay and understand the answer.
days.paretoFocus: Money is where a visitor is most exposed. Four phrases cover almost every counter in the country, and multibanco is the word nobody teaches you.
drills: Ask the price of three things around you, out loud, in Portuguese.
Say how you would like to pay, both ways, without looking.
Practise the whole till exchange from price to change.

items: How do you ask what something costs?
What does multibanco mean?
How do you ask for change for a twenty?

activities.title: Paying
activities.intro: The phrases that decide how much you pay and how.

items.en: How much does this cost?
Do you take cards?
Do you take debit cards?
items.note: Multibanco is the Portuguese bank-card network. The word is used for the card, the machine and the ATM.

items.en: I prefer to pay in cash.
Do you have change for twenty euros?
It is very expensive.

items.hr: Queria a fatura, se faz favor.
items.en: I would like the receipt, please.
items.note: Ask for it with your tax number if you have one, for the deduction.

items.en: It works out cheaper this way.

activities.title: At the till
activities.intro: Choose what to say at the till.

questions.prompt: You have no cash. You ask:
questions.explanation: Aceita cartão? asks whether cards are taken. Many small places still prefer cash.

questions.prompt: Multibanco is:
options: The Portuguese bank-card and ATM network
questions.answer: The Portuguese bank-card and ATM network
questions.explanation: You will see the word on cash machines and on card terminals everywhere.

questions.prompt: You want to pay with notes and coins. You say:
questions.explanation: Em dinheiro means in cash.

questions.prompt: You hand over a twenty for something small. You ask:
questions.explanation: Troco is change. Small cafés often ask for something smaller.

activities.title: Buying a souvenir
activities.intro: Buying a small souvenir. Read both parts, then only Me.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Boa tarde. Quanto custa isto?
lines.en: Good afternoon. How much does this cost?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: São doze euros.
lines.en: That is twelve euros.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Aceita multibanco?
lines.en: Do you take debit cards?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Aceitamos, sim. Ou dinheiro.
lines.en: Yes we do. Or cash.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Prefiro pagar em dinheiro.
lines.en: I prefer to pay in cash.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Com certeza.
lines.en: Of course.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tem troco de vinte euros?
lines.en: Do you have change for twenty euros?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tenho. Aqui está o troco.
lines.en: I do. Here is your change.

days.title: Where is it?
days.objective: You will ask the way and understand the four directions you get back.
days.paretoFocus: Getting lost is the most likely thing to go wrong on a visit, and the answers you will hear are a very short list: right, left, straight on, and how far.
drills: Ask where three real places near you are, out loud.
Say the three directions without looking at them.
Give somebody directions to your own front door in Portuguese.

items: How do you ask where something is?
What does sempre em frente mean?
How would a woman say she is lost?

activities.title: Asking the way
activities.intro: Ask, then understand. The second half is what most phrasebooks leave out.

items.en: Where is the station?
items.note: Onde fica works for any place. Swap the last word.

items.en: Turn right.
Turn left.
Keep straight on.
Is it far from here?
items.note: Fica is the same verb as in onde fica, so the pair travels together.

items.hr: Fica a cinco minutos a pé.
items.en: It is five minutes on foot.
I am lost.
items.note: A woman says estou perdida.

items.en: Can you show me on the map?

activities.title: Following directions
activities.intro: Match what you hear to what you do.

questions.prompt: Somebody tells you 'Siga sempre em frente'. You:
questions.explanation: Sempre em frente is straight ahead, always.

questions.prompt: You want to know if it is walkable. You ask:
questions.explanation: The answer often comes as minutes rather than distance.

questions.prompt: 'Fica a cinco minutos a pé' means:
questions.explanation: A pé is on foot.

questions.prompt: A woman who is lost says:
questions.explanation: Adjectives agree with the speaker, so she says perdida.

activities.title: Towards the station
activities.intro: You ask a passer-by for the station. Read it aloud twice.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Desculpe. Onde fica a estação?
lines.en: Excuse me. Where is the station?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Siga sempre em frente.
lines.en: Keep straight on.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Fica longe daqui?
lines.en: Is it far from here?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Não. Fica a cinco minutos a pé.
lines.en: No. It is five minutes on foot.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: E depois?
lines.en: And then?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Depois vire à direita.
lines.en: Then turn right.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Pode mostrar-me no mapa?
lines.en: Can you show me on the map?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Claro. É aqui.
lines.en: Of course. It is here.

days.title: Catching the bus
days.objective: You will buy a ticket, check you are on the right service and know when it leaves.
days.paretoFocus: Portugal is easy to travel and hard to ask about: the words for ticket, stop and departure are the ones that strand you if you do not have them.
drills: Buy a ticket out loud to somewhere you actually want to go.
Ask the departure time three different ways round the same phrase.
Say the difference between estação and paragem without looking.

items: How do you ask for a return ticket?
How do you check a bus goes where you want?
What does paragem mean?

activities.title: Tickets and times
activities.intro: Buying and boarding. Each phrase is one you will use at a counter or a door.

items.hr: Um bilhete para o Porto, se faz favor.
items.en: One ticket to Porto, please.

items.hr: Quero um bilhete de ida e volta.
items.en: I want a return ticket.
items.note: Só de ida is one way.

items.hr: A que horas parte o comboio?
items.en: What time does the train leave?
Does this bus go to Belém?
Where is the bus stop?

items.hr: O metro fecha à uma da manhã.
items.en: The metro closes at one in the morning.
I am getting off at the next one.
I missed the train.

activities.title: At the station
activities.intro: One phrase per situation.

questions.prompt: You want to come back the same day. You ask for:
options: Um bilhete de ida e volta.
questions.answer: Um bilhete de ida e volta.
questions.explanation: Ida e volta is there and back. Só de ida is one way.

questions.prompt: You are unsure the bus is the right one. You ask:
options: A que horas parte o comboio?
questions.explanation: Ask the driver as you board. A nod is all you need back.

questions.prompt: 'Desço na próxima' tells the driver you:
options: Are getting off at the next stop
Are going to the last stop
questions.answer: Are getting off at the next stop
questions.explanation: Useful on a crowded bus where the door is far away.

questions.prompt: Paragem means:
questions.explanation: Estação is a station; paragem is the stop in the street.

activities.title: Buying a ticket
activities.intro: At the ticket window. Read both parts, then only Me.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Boa tarde. Um bilhete para o Porto, se faz favor.
lines.en: Good afternoon. One ticket to Porto, please.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Só de ida?
lines.en: One way?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Quero um bilhete de ida e volta.
lines.en: I want a return ticket.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: São trinta e dois euros.
lines.en: That is thirty-two euros.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A que horas parte o comboio?
lines.en: What time does the train leave?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Às quinze e dez, na linha dois.
lines.en: At fifteen ten, on platform two.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Obrigado. E onde fica a paragem?
lines.en: Thank you. And where is the bus stop?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: À saída, à direita.
lines.en: At the exit, on the right.

days.title: Eating out
days.objective: You will get a table, order, say what you do not eat and pay.
days.paretoFocus: A restaurant is the one place a visitor cannot avoid speaking, and the one where getting it slightly wrong costs you a meal you did not want.
drills: Order a full meal out loud, starter to bill.
Name one thing you never eat, in a single Portuguese sentence.
Decide in Portuguese whether to accept the couvert.

items: What is the menu called in Portugal?
How do you say you do not eat meat?
What is the couvert and is it free?

activities.title: At the table
activities.intro: From the door to the bill, in eight phrases.

items.hr: Uma mesa para dois, se faz favor.
items.en: A table for two, please.
The menu, please.
items.note: Ementa in Portugal. Cardápio is Brazilian.

items.hr: Qual é o prato do dia?
items.en: What is the dish of the day?
I am vegetarian.
items.note: A woman says sou vegetariana.

items.en: I do not eat meat.

items.hr: Mais um copo de água, se faz favor.
items.en: One more glass of water, please.
It was all very good.
Can we pay together?

activities.title: Ordering well
activities.intro: Choose the phrase that avoids the misunderstanding.

questions.prompt: In Portugal the menu is called:
questions.explanation: Cardápio is understood but marks you as having learned Brazilian Portuguese.

questions.prompt: You eat fish but not meat. You say:
options: Qual é o prato do dia?
questions.explanation: Sou vegetariano would also rule out the fish you actually want.

questions.prompt: The bread and starters put on your table without asking:
options: Are charged unless you send them back
Are part of the main course
questions.answer: Are charged unless you send them back
questions.explanation: The couvert is normal and legal. Wave it away if you do not want it.

questions.prompt: You want one bill for everyone. You ask:
options: Mais um copo de água, se faz favor.
Uma mesa para dois, se faz favor.
questions.explanation: Splitting is em separado, which many small places would rather avoid.

activities.title: Dinner
activities.intro: Dinner in a small tasca. Read it twice.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Boa noite. Uma mesa para dois, se faz favor.
lines.en: Good evening. A table for two, please.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Com certeza. Aqui têm.
lines.en: Of course. Here you are.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A ementa, se faz favor.
lines.en: The menu, please.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Aqui está. O prato do dia é bacalhau.
lines.en: Here it is. The dish of the day is cod.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Não como carne. Isso é peixe?
lines.en: I do not eat meat. Is that fish?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: É peixe, sim.
lines.en: It is fish, yes.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Então quero isso. Estava tudo muito bom.
lines.en: Then I want that. It was all very good.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Fico contente. A conta já vem.
lines.en: I am glad. The bill is coming.

days.title: Going shopping
days.objective: You will browse without being pressured, try something on and understand opening hours.
days.paretoFocus: Shops here run on different hours from most of Europe, and só estou a ver is the phrase that buys you room to look.
drills: Turn down help politely, out loud, three times.
Ask for a different size and a different colour without looking.
Say when your local shop opens and closes, in Portuguese.

items: How do you say you are just looking?
What are you being asked with precisa de saco?
What does ao domingo tell you about a shop?

activities.title: In the store
activities.intro: Browsing, trying, buying, and knowing when the door will be open.

items.en: I am just looking, thank you.
Do you have another size?
Can I try it on?
Do you have it in another colour?
I will take this one.
Do you need a bag?
items.note: You will be asked this, and bags are charged for.

items.en: What time do you open?
It is closed on Sundays.

activities.title: Among the shelves
activities.intro: The right phrase keeps the assistant helpful.

questions.prompt: An assistant approaches and you want to browse. You say:
questions.explanation: It is polite, not dismissive, and it is exactly what a Portuguese shopper says.

questions.prompt: 'Precisa de saco?' is asking whether you:
questions.explanation: Bags are charged for, so the answer is a real decision.

questions.prompt: You want to try something on. You ask:
questions.explanation: Experimentar covers trying on clothes and trying out anything else.

questions.prompt: Many smaller Portuguese shops:
options: Close on Sunday and at lunchtime
questions.answer: Close on Sunday and at lunchtime
questions.explanation: Outside the big centres, ao domingo means shut.

activities.title: A jumper
activities.intro: Buying a jumper. Read both parts, then only Me.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Boa tarde. Precisa de ajuda?
lines.en: Good afternoon. Do you need help?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Só estou a ver, obrigado.
lines.en: I am just looking, thank you.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Esteja à vontade.
lines.en: Make yourself at home.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tem outro tamanho?
lines.en: Do you have another size?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tenho, em eme. Quer experimentar?
lines.en: I do, in medium. Want to try it?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Posso experimentar?
lines.en: Can I try it on?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Claro. Ali ao fundo.
lines.en: Of course. At the back there.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Levo este. Precisa de saco?
lines.en: I will take this one. Do you need a bag?

days.title: I do not understand
days.objective: You will keep a conversation alive when you have lost it, which matters more than any single word.
days.paretoFocus: Every beginner stalls. The difference between a visitor who improves and one who gives up is having six phrases that ask for the sentence again, slower.
drills: Say the six repair phrases without looking at them.
Point at five things around you and ask how each is said.
Use ainda estou a aprender in a real conversation today.

items: How do you ask somebody to slow down?
Which verb do the Portuguese use for understanding?
How do you ask what a word means?

activities.title: Buying time
activities.intro: Repair phrases. Learn these before you learn more vocabulary.

items.en: I do not understand.
items.note: Percebo, not entendo, is the Portuguese habit.

items.en: Could you repeat that, please?
Could you speak more slowly?

items.hr: Como se diz isto em português?
items.en: How do you say this in Portuguese?
What does this word mean?
Could you write it down here?
I understand a little.
I am still learning.
items.note: This one sentence usually makes people slow down and stay in Portuguese.

activities.title: When you get stuck
activities.intro: Pick the phrase that gets the conversation moving again.

questions.prompt: They spoke too fast. You say:
options: Como se diz isto em português?
questions.explanation: Devagar is slowly. It asks for pace, not for a translation.

questions.prompt: You point at an object you cannot name. You ask:
options: Como se diz isto em português?
questions.answer: Como se diz isto em português?
questions.explanation: It turns any object in front of you into a free vocabulary lesson.

questions.prompt: In Portugal, 'I understand' is usually:
questions.explanation: All are correct Portuguese, but percebo is what you will hear here.

questions.prompt: Which sentence most reliably keeps somebody speaking Portuguese to you?
questions.explanation: It explains the pauses and invites patience instead of a switch to English.

activities.title: Lost in conversation
activities.intro: Somebody answers faster than you can follow. Read it twice.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: O comboio sai da linha três, mas hoje mudou.
lines.en: The train leaves from platform three, but today it changed.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Desculpe. Não percebo.
lines.en: Sorry. I do not understand.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Mudou de linha. Hoje é a linha cinco.
lines.en: It changed platform. Today it is platform five.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Pode falar mais devagar?
lines.en: Could you speak more slowly?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Cla-ro. Li-nha cin-co.
lines.en: Of course. Plat-form five.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Percebo um pouco. Pode escrever aqui?
lines.en: I understand a little. Could you write it down here?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Aqui tem. Linha cinco.
lines.en: Here you go. Platform five.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Obrigado. Ainda estou a aprender.
lines.en: Thank you. I am still learning.

days.title: I need help
days.objective: You will ask for help, find a pharmacy or a toilet, and say what has gone wrong.
days.paretoFocus: These are the phrases you hope not to need, which is exactly why they have to be automatic rather than looked up.
drills: Say the emergency number out loud in Portuguese.
Say all four help phrases without looking.
Find the nearest farmácia to you and ask the way to it in Portuguese.

items: What number do you call in an emergency?
How do you ask for the toilet in Portugal?
What can a farmácia do for you?

activities.title: Emergencies
activities.intro: Say each one out loud now, so it is there if you ever need it.

items.en: I need help.

items.hr: Onde fica a casa de banho?
items.en: Where is the toilet?

items.hr: Chame um médico, se faz favor.
items.en: Call a doctor, please.

items.hr: Onde fica a farmácia mais próxima?
items.en: Where is the nearest pharmacy?
I have lost my passport.
I do not feel well.
Call 112.
items.note: 112 is the emergency number across the European Union.

items.en: Could you call the police?

activities.title: In an emergency
activities.intro: One phrase per emergency.

questions.prompt: The emergency number in Portugal is:
questions.explanation: 112 works across the European Union and reaches all three services.

questions.prompt: In Portugal you ask for the toilet as:
questions.explanation: Banheiro is Brazilian, and a sanita is the toilet bowl itself.

questions.prompt: You feel unwell in a shop. You say:
questions.explanation: It is the normal way to say it and it will get you a chair and water.

questions.prompt: A Portuguese farmácia, unlike most shops:
options: Can advise and dispense for minor problems
questions.answer: Can advise and dispense for minor problems
questions.explanation: The pharmacist is the usual first stop before a doctor here.

activities.title: At the pharmacy
activities.intro: You are unwell and go to the pharmacy. Read both parts, then only Me.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Boa tarde. Não me sinto bem.
lines.en: Good afternoon. I do not feel well.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: O que tem?

lines.speaker: Me

lines.hr: Tem dores?
lines.en: Are you in pain?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Não sei. Chame um médico, se faz favor.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Calma. Sente-se aqui.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Onde fica a casa de banho?
lines.en: Where is the toilet?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ao fundo, à esquerda.

days.title: A0 checkpoint
days.objective: You will put the ten days together and run the transactions end to end, from memory.
days.paretoFocus: This is the checkpoint: if you can do these without looking, you can spend a week in Portugal without switching to English at every counter.
drills: Run the café transaction end to end without looking, twice.
Do the same for the ticket counter and the restaurant door.
Spend one whole real transaction today without switching to English.

items: Order a coffee and a pastry from memory.
Ask for the total and offer to pay by card.
Ask somebody to repeat something more slowly.

activities.title: All together

lines.en: So our tidying up is almost done.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Falta só a minha secretária.
lines.en: Only my desk is left.

days.title: Where things are: prepositions of place
days.objective: Say exactly where something or someone is using place prepositions and their contractions.
days.paretoFocus: Finding things, giving directions inside a building and describing a room all depend on this small set of prepositions.
drills: Describe where five objects are in the room you are in right now.
Say the same five sentences again, but move each object somewhere else.
Draw a simple map of your street and say where three shops are in relation to each other.

items: What happens when de meets the articles o, a, os, as?
Give the phrase for 'on top of' and the phrase for 'under'.
Which verb do you use for the fixed location of a building?

activities.title: On top, underneath, beside
activities.intro: Most Portuguese place expressions end in 'de', and that 'de' merges with the article that follows: de plus o gives do, de plus a gives da. Use 'estar' for temporary position and 'ficar' for where a building is located.

items.hr: O livro está em cima da mesa.
items.en: The book is on the table.
items.note: em cima de plus a gives em cima da

items.hr: As chaves estão dentro da gaveta.
items.en: The keys are inside the drawer.

items.hr: O gato está debaixo do sofá.
items.en: The cat is under the sofa.
items.note: de plus o gives do

items.hr: A farmácia fica ao lado do banco.
items.en: The pharmacy is next to the bank.
items.note: ficar is normal for fixed locations

items.hr: O carro está entre a árvore e o muro.
items.en: The car is between the tree and the wall.
items.note: entre takes no de

activities.title: Where exactly is it?
activities.intro: Practise place prepositions together with the right contraction.

questions.prompt: Which phrase means 'under the bed': 'A mala está ___ cama.'
questions.explanation: debaixo de means under, and de plus a cama gives da cama.

questions.prompt: What is the correct contraction of de plus os?
questions.explanation: de merges with the masculine plural article os to give dos.

questions.prompt: Fill in the contraction of de and the feminine article: 'O comboio está à frente ___ estação.'
questions.explanation: estação is feminine, so de plus a becomes da.

questions.prompt: Fill in the two words that mean 'beside': 'O museu fica ___ ___ do teatro.'
questions.explanation: The expression is ao lado de, and here de plus o teatro gives do teatro.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'The keys are inside the bag.'
questions.explanation: estar gives temporary position and dentro de plus a mala contracts to dentro da mala.

questions.prompt: Listen, then type the missing word: 'O ___ está em cima da mesa.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'O livro está em cima da mesa.', which means 'The book is on the table.'
questions.audioText: O livro está em cima da mesa.

questions.prompt: Put this into Portuguese: 'The car is between the tree and the wall.'
questions.answer: O carro está entre a árvore e o muro.
questions.explanation: 'The car is between the tree and the wall.' is 'O carro está entre a árvore e o muro.'

activities.title: Looking for the glasses
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Someone at home cannot find their glasses, so guide them using place prepositions.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Não encontro os meus óculos. Sabes onde estão?
lines.en: I cannot find my glasses. Do you know where they are?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Acho que estão em cima da mesa da cozinha.
lines.en: I think they are on the kitchen table.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Aqui não estão. E debaixo dos jornais?
lines.en: They are not here. What about under the newspapers?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Também não. Vê dentro da tua mochila.
lines.en: Not there either. Look inside your rucksack.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Já vi. Nada.
lines.en: I have looked. Nothing.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Então estão ao lado do computador, entre os livros.
lines.en: Then they are next to the computer, between the books.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Encontrei! Estavam mesmo aí.
lines.en: Found them! They were right there.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Da próxima vez, deixa-os atrás do telefone.
lines.en: Next time, leave them behind the phone.

days.title: Colours and describing objects
days.objective: Describe an object by its colour, size and material with adjectives that agree correctly.
days.paretoFocus: Colour plus one more adjective is enough to identify almost any object you need to point out, buy or ask about.
drills: Pick eight objects near you and say the colour of each one out loud.
Add a second adjective of size or shape to four of those sentences.
Describe a bag you own in three sentences without naming the brand.

items: Which colours keep the same form for masculine and feminine?
How do you make the plural of azul?
Where does a colour adjective normally go, before or after the noun?

activities.title: What colour is it?
activities.intro: Colour adjectives come after the noun and agree with it. Colours ending in -o change to -a in the feminine, while colours like verde and azul have one form for both genders. In the plural, azul becomes azuis.

items.en: This jacket is blue.
items.note: azul is the same for both genders; plural azuis

items.en: The red jumper is mine.
items.note: vermelho becomes vermelha before a feminine noun

items.hr: Tenho uns sapatos castanhos muito velhos.
items.en: I have some very old brown shoes.

items.hr: A parede é branca e o chão é cinzento.
items.en: The wall is white and the floor is grey.

items.hr: Comprei uma pasta verde e leve.
items.en: I bought a light green folder.
items.note: verde never changes for gender

activities.title: Colours and agreement
activities.intro: Practise making colour adjectives agree with the noun they describe.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct agreement for 'red': 'uma mala ___'.
questions.explanation: mala is feminine singular, so the -o ending changes to -a.

questions.prompt: Which colour has exactly the same form for masculine and feminine?
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in -e do not change for gender: um carro verde, uma porta verde.

questions.prompt: Fill in the plural colour meaning 'blue': 'Os olhos dela são ___.'
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in -l change -l to -is in the plural.

questions.prompt: Fill in the colour of snow, agreeing with the feminine noun: 'A neve é ___.'
questions.explanation: neve is feminine, so the adjective takes the -a ending.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'I have a black jacket.'
questions.explanation: The colour follows the noun and agrees with it in gender and number.

questions.prompt: Listen and fill in the word you hear: 'Este ___ é azul.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Este casaco é azul.', which means 'This jacket is blue.'

questions.prompt: Type the Portuguese for: 'I bought a light green folder.'
questions.answer: Comprei uma pasta verde e leve.
questions.explanation: 'I bought a light green folder.' is 'Comprei uma pasta verde e leve.'

activities.title: O guarda-chuva perdido
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. You lost an umbrella and an employee at the lost property counter needs a description, so use colours and other object adjectives.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Boa tarde. Perdeu alguma coisa?
lines.en: Good afternoon. Did you lose something?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sim, perdi o meu guarda-chuva ontem.
lines.en: Yes, I lost my umbrella yesterday.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: De que cor é?
lines.en: What colour is it?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: É azul escuro, com o cabo castanho.
lines.en: It is dark blue, with a brown handle.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Temos dois. Um é grande e outro é pequeno.
lines.en: We have two. One is big and the other is small.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: O meu é pequeno e tem uma fita branca.
lines.en: Mine is small and has a white ribbon.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Então é este. Confirme, se faz favor.
lines.en: Then this is the one. Please confirm.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: É esse mesmo. Muito obrigado!
lines.en: That is exactly the one. Thank you very much!

days.title: Days, months and dates
days.objective: Name the days and months and say or write a full date the Portuguese way.
days.paretoFocus: Dates appear in every appointment, ticket, form and birthday, and the Portuguese pattern is different enough from English to cause real confusion.
drills: Say the seven days of the week out loud without stopping, twice.
Say the twelve months in order, then say the month of three birthdays you know.
Write today's date in full Portuguese, then next Monday's date.

items: Why are most Portuguese weekdays built on numbers?
Do months take a capital letter in Portuguese?
Which small word goes before a month name to say when something happens?

activities.title: What day is it today?
activities.intro: Portuguese weekdays are counted: segunda-feira is the second day, terça-feira the third, and so on to sexta-feira, then sábado and domingo. Months are written in lower case. A date is built as day number plus de plus month plus de plus year.

items.en: Today is Monday.
items.note: in speech people often drop the -feira: hoje é segunda

items.hr: A reunião é na quarta-feira de manhã.
items.en: The meeting is on Wednesday morning.
items.note: em plus a gives na before a weekday

items.hr: O meu aniversário é a 12 de maio.
items.en: My birthday is on the twelfth of May.
items.note: months are lower case in Portuguese

items.hr: Em agosto, muita gente vai de férias.
items.en: In August, a lot of people go on holiday.
items.note: em plus month for a whole month

items.hr: Hoje é dia 3 de outubro de 2026.
items.en: Today is the third of October 2026.
items.note: the full pattern is dia, number, de, month, de, year

activities.title: Dias, meses e datas
activities.intro: Practise weekday names, month names and the shape of a Portuguese date.

questions.prompt: Which word means Thursday?
questions.explanation: Counting from domingo as the first day, Thursday is the fifth, so quinta-feira.

questions.prompt: How are month names normally written in Portuguese?
options: With an accent on the first vowel
questions.explanation: Unlike English, Portuguese writes janeiro, fevereiro and the rest in lower case.

questions.prompt: Fill in the one word preposition used before a month name: 'O curso começa ___ setembro.'
questions.explanation: For a whole month you use em: em setembro, em janeiro.

questions.prompt: Fill in the weekday that comes after sexta-feira: 'Depois de sexta-feira vem o ___.'
questions.explanation: The weekend days sábado and domingo keep their old names instead of a number.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'My birthday is on the fifteenth of June.'
questions.explanation: A specific date uses a plus the number plus de plus the month in lower case.

questions.prompt: Play the audio and complete: 'Hoje é ___-feira.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Hoje é segunda-feira.', which means 'Today is Monday.'

questions.prompt: Write it in Portuguese: 'Today is the third of October 2026.'
questions.answer: Hoje é dia 3 de outubro de 2026.
questions.explanation: 'Today is the third of October 2026.' is 'Hoje é dia 3 de outubro de 2026.'

activities.title: Marcar a data
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A colleague wants to fix the date of a birthday lunch, so answer with weekdays, months and full dates.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Quando é o teu aniversário?
lines.en: When is your birthday?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: É a 20 de novembro.
lines.en: It is on the twentieth of November.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E esse dia cai em que dia da semana?
lines.en: And what day of the week does that fall on?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Cai numa sexta-feira, felizmente.
lines.en: It falls on a Friday, luckily.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Então almoçamos juntos nesse dia?
lines.en: Shall we have lunch together that day?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Prefiro no sábado, dia 21, se puderes.
lines.en: I would rather do it on Saturday the twenty first, if you can.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sábado é perfeito. Fica marcado.
lines.en: Saturday is perfect. It is settled.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ótimo. 21 de novembro, ao meio-dia.
lines.en: Great. The twenty first of November, at midday.

days.title: Big numbers and prices
days.objective: Understand and say prices, large numbers and totals in euros and cents.
days.paretoFocus: Hearing a price correctly is the difference between paying confidently and guessing, and large numbers also cover rents, salaries and years.
drills: Say the numbers 100, 200, 500, 1000 and 1500 out loud in Portuguese.
Read five prices you can see today as Portuguese euro and cent amounts.
Ask and answer 'how much is it in total' three times with different figures.

items: When do you say cem and when do you say cento?
How do the hundreds change before a feminine noun?
How do you read an amount that has both euros and cents?

activities.title: Quanto custa?
activities.intro: Exactly one hundred is cem, but anything above it uses cento: cento e um, cento e vinte. From two hundred upwards the hundreds agree in gender: duzentos euros, duzentas pessoas. Prices are read as euros, then e, then the cents.

items.en: This jacket costs fifty euros.
items.note: custar is the normal verb for to cost

items.hr: O bilhete custa dois euros e trinta cêntimos.
items.en: The ticket costs two euros thirty.
items.note: 2,30 EUR is read dois euros e trinta

items.hr: O computador custa mil e duzentos euros.
items.en: The computer costs one thousand two hundred euros.
items.note: mil never takes um in front

items.hr: A renda é setecentos euros por mês.
items.en: The rent is seven hundred euros a month.

items.hr: Quanto é ao todo? São vinte e cinco euros.
items.en: How much is it altogether? It is twenty five euros.
items.note: ao todo means in total

activities.title: Numbers and prices
activities.intro: Practise reading large numbers and euro amounts.

questions.prompt: How do you say exactly 100 on its own?
questions.explanation: cem is used for exactly one hundred; cento only appears with something after it.

questions.prompt: Which form means 200 before a feminine noun such as pessoas?
questions.explanation: From 200 up, the hundreds agree in gender, so duzentas pessoas.

questions.prompt: Fill in the Portuguese word for the number 1000: 'O curso custa ___ euros.'
questions.explanation: One thousand is simply mil, with no article before it.

questions.prompt: Fill in the question word for asking a total: '___ é ao todo?'
questions.explanation: Quanto asks how much, and ao todo adds the sense of altogether.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'It costs one thousand five hundred altogether.'
questions.explanation: mil takes no article, e joins it to the hundreds, and ao todo means in total.

questions.prompt: Listen closely and fill the gap: 'Este casaco custa ___ euros.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Este casaco custa cinquenta euros.', which means 'This jacket costs fifty euros.'

questions.prompt: Say it in Portuguese, in writing: 'How much is it altogether? It is twenty five euros.'
questions.answer: Quanto é ao todo? São vinte e cinco euros.
questions.explanation: 'How much is it altogether? It is twenty five euros.' is 'Quanto é ao todo? São vinte e cinco euros.'

activities.title: Renting a bicycle
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. You are renting a bicycle and need to check prices, so use numbers, euros and cents.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Boa tarde. Quer alugar uma bicicleta?
lines.en: Good afternoon. Do you want to rent a bicycle?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sim. Quanto custa por dia?
lines.en: Yes. How much does it cost per day?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: São quinze euros por dia ou oitenta por semana.
lines.en: It is fifteen euros a day or eighty for a week.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: E o capacete é à parte?
lines.en: And is the helmet extra?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: É, custa dois euros e cinquenta cêntimos.
lines.en: It is, it costs two euros fifty.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Levo a bicicleta por três dias e um capacete.
lines.en: I will take the bicycle for three days and one helmet.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Então são quarenta e sete euros e cinquenta ao todo.
lines.en: So it is forty seven euros fifty altogether.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Perfeito. Aqui estão cinquenta euros.
lines.en: Perfect. Here is fifty euros.

days.title: Poder, querer e dever: os verbos modais
days.objective: Express ability, permission, wishes and obligation with poder, querer and dever plus an infinitive.
days.paretoFocus: These three verbs let you build hundreds of new sentences from verbs you already know, without learning any new tense.
drills: Ask for permission to do five different things using poder.
Say three things you want to do this week and three things you should do.
Turn five simple present sentences into modal sentences by adding poder or dever.

items: Which form of the second verb follows a modal?
Give the eu and nós forms of poder.
Which of the three verbs expresses obligation or advice?

activities.title: Posso, quero, devo
activities.intro: Poder means can or may, querer means to want, and dever means should or must. All three are followed directly by an infinitive with no preposition in between. Their present forms are slightly irregular, so learn them as blocks.

items.en: May I open the window?
items.note: poder: posso, podes, pode, podemos, podem

items.hr: Queres um café ou preferes um chá?
items.en: Do you want a coffee or do you prefer a tea?
items.note: querer: quero, queres, quer, queremos, querem

items.hr: Devemos chegar às oito em ponto.
items.en: We should arrive at eight sharp.
items.note: dever: devo, deves, deve, devemos, devem

items.en: You cannot park here.
items.note: não goes before the whole verb group

items.hr: Ele quer aprender a conduzir este ano.
items.en: He wants to learn to drive this year.

activities.title: Modal verbs in the present
activities.intro: Practise the present forms of poder, querer and dever.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form meaning 'I want': 'Eu ___ falar contigo.'
questions.explanation: The eu form of querer is quero, and the next verb stays in the infinitive.

questions.prompt: Which of these verbs expresses obligation or strong advice?
questions.explanation: dever covers should and must; poder is ability or permission and querer is desire.

questions.prompt: Fill in the eu form of the verb poder: '___ ajudar-te com as malas?'
questions.explanation: The eu form is irregular and changes the stem vowel to o.

questions.prompt: Fill in the nós form of the verb dever: '___ falar com o professor amanhã.'
questions.explanation: dever is a regular -ER verb in the nós form, taking the -emos ending.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'We cannot pay by card here.'
questions.explanation: não comes before the modal, and the second verb stays in the infinitive.

questions.prompt: Type the word you hear: 'Posso abrir a ___?'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Posso abrir a janela?', which means 'May I open the window?'

questions.prompt: Put this into Portuguese: 'He wants to learn to drive this year.'
questions.answer: Ele quer aprender a conduzir este ano.
questions.explanation: 'He wants to learn to drive this year.' is 'Ele quer aprender a conduzir este ano.'

activities.title: At the reception desk
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. You are at a reception desk asking for permission and saying what you want and should do, using the three modal verbs.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Bom dia. Em que posso ajudar?
lines.en: Good morning. How can I help?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Posso deixar aqui a mala até às três?
lines.en: May I leave my suitcase here until three?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Pode, sim. Mas deve levar os documentos consigo.
lines.en: Yes, you may. But you should take your documents with you.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro. Também quero saber onde fica a paragem.
lines.en: Of course. I also want to know where the stop is.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Fica ali à esquerda. Quer um mapa?
lines.en: It is over there on the left. Do you want a map?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Quero, obrigado. A que horas devo voltar?
lines.en: Yes I do, thank you. What time should I come back?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Deve voltar antes das seis, porque fechamos.
lines.en: You should come back before six, because we close.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Combinado. Posso pagar agora?
lines.en: Agreed. May I pay now?

days.title: Reflexive verbs: chamar-se, levantar-se, deitar-se
days.objective: Use reflexive verbs correctly, including where the pronoun goes in positive and negative sentences.
days.paretoFocus: Reflexive verbs cover names, getting up, going to bed, feeling and remembering, and European Portuguese places the pronoun differently from Brazilian usage.
drills: Say your own name and two other people's names with chamar-se.
Describe your morning with three reflexive verbs in the eu form.
Turn three of those sentences into the negative and move the pronoun.

items: Where does the pronoun go in a normal affirmative sentence?
What changes about the pronoun when the sentence is negative?
Which pronoun goes with eu and which goes with tu?

activities.title: Chamo-me, levanto-me, deito-me
activities.intro: Reflexive verbs carry a pronoun: me, te, se, nos, se. In European Portuguese the pronoun normally follows the verb and is joined with a hyphen. It moves in front of the verb after a negative word, a question word or words like que, quando and já.

items.hr: Chamo-me Ana e sou de Faro.
items.en: My name is Ana and I am from Faro.
items.note: the pronoun follows the verb with a hyphen

items.en: I get up at seven in the morning.

items.hr: Ela deita-se cedo durante a semana.
items.en: She goes to bed early during the week.
items.note: third person pronoun is se

items.hr: Não me lembro do nome dele.
items.en: I do not remember his name.
items.note: after não the pronoun comes before the verb

items.hr: A que horas te levantas ao sábado?
items.en: What time do you get up on Saturdays?
items.note: a question word also pulls the pronoun forward

activities.title: Where does the pronoun go?
activities.intro: Practise reflexive pronouns and their position in the sentence.

questions.prompt: In a negative sentence, where does the reflexive pronoun go?
options: After the verb with a hyphen
At the end of the sentence
questions.explanation: Negative words attract the pronoun to the position in front of the verb.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct European Portuguese?
questions.explanation: In an ordinary affirmative sentence the pronoun follows the verb and is hyphenated.

questions.prompt: Fill in the missing reflexive pronoun for eu: 'Levanto-___ às sete.'
questions.explanation: The first person singular reflexive pronoun is me.

questions.prompt: Fill in the two words that give the tu form of chamar-se: 'Como ___ ___?'
questions.explanation: The question word Como pulls the pronoun in front of the verb, giving te chamas.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'I go to bed at midnight every day.'
questions.explanation: With no negative or question word, the pronoun stays attached after the verb.

questions.prompt: Listen and complete the sentence: 'Levanto-me às sete da ___.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Levanto-me às sete da manhã.', which means 'I get up at seven in the morning.'

questions.prompt: Type the Portuguese for: 'What time do you get up on Saturdays?'
questions.answer: A que horas te levantas ao sábado?
questions.explanation: 'What time do you get up on Saturdays?' is 'A que horas te levantas ao sábado?'

activities.title: The new housemate
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A new flatmate is comparing schedules with you, so use reflexive verbs in both affirmative and negative sentences.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Desculpa, como te chamas?
lines.en: Sorry, what is your name?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Chamo-me Rui. E tu?
lines.en: My name is Rui. And you?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sofia. A que horas te levantas?
lines.en: Sofia. What time do you get up?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Levanto-me às seis e meia, porque trabalho longe.
lines.en: I get up at half past six, because I work far away.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Eu não me levanto tão cedo.
lines.en: I do not get up that early.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: E deitas-te tarde?
lines.en: And do you go to bed late?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Deito-me quase sempre à meia-noite.
lines.en: I almost always go to bed at midnight.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Então nunca nos encontramos de manhã.
lines.en: So we never meet in the morning.

days.title: Asking politely: se faz favor, queria, pode dizer-me
days.objective: Make requests that sound polite to a Portuguese ear instead of blunt or demanding.
days.paretoFocus: The same request can sound rude or friendly depending on three or four fixed formulas, and these formulas work in shops, streets and offices alike.
drills: Turn five direct commands into polite requests using the softer wanting form.
Stop three imaginary strangers and ask each a different question politely.
Practise apologising first, then asking, five times in a row.

items: Which softened form of querer do you use when ordering?
What is the everyday word for please in Portugal?
Which verb starts a polite request for help?

activities.title: Pedidos delicados
activities.intro: Portuguese softens requests in three ways: adding se faz favor, replacing quero with the gentler queria, and opening with a verb like pode or importa-se de. Starting with desculpe before you ask a stranger is almost obligatory.

items.en: A coffee, please.
items.note: se faz favor is the usual polite phrase in Portugal

items.hr: Queria um bilhete para o Porto.
items.en: I would like a ticket to Porto.
items.note: queria is softer than quero

items.hr: Pode dizer-me onde fica a estação?
items.en: Can you tell me where the station is?
Would you mind closing the door?
items.note: importar-se de plus infinitive is a very polite request

items.en: Excuse me, can you repeat that more slowly?

activities.title: Excuse me, and please
activities.intro: Practise choosing the polite version of a request.

questions.prompt: Which version sounds politest when ordering in a shop?
questions.explanation: queria softens the request; quero can sound blunt and a bare noun is abrupt.

questions.prompt: Which phrase is the everyday way to say please in Portugal?
questions.explanation: de nada answers thanks, com licença asks to pass and não faz mal means never mind.

questions.prompt: Fill in the você form of the verb poder to open a polite request: '___ ajudar-me, se faz favor?'
questions.explanation: The third person form is used for polite address, giving Pode ajudar-me.

questions.prompt: Fill in the word you say first to get a stranger's attention politely: '___, sabe que horas são?'
questions.explanation: Desculpe apologises for interrupting and is the standard opener with strangers.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'I would like a ticket to Lisbon, please.'
questions.explanation: The polite formula comes at the end, after the complete request.

days.title: At the restaurant: ordering, commenting and paying
days.objective: Get a table, order a full meal, comment on the food and ask for the bill.
days.paretoFocus: A restaurant visit follows a fixed script, so learning the six or seven key lines makes the whole situation predictable.
drills: Say out loud the three lines you need to be seated and to see the menu.
Order a starter, a main course and a drink for yourself in one breath.
Practise two comments on the food and two ways of asking for the bill.

items: What is the Portuguese word used in Portugal for the menu?
Which phrase do you use to say what you personally will have?
How do you ask for the bill politely?

activities.title: A meal out
activities.intro: In Portugal the menu is called a ementa. Waiters take the order table by table, so you mark your own choice with para mim. Comments on food use estar, because the taste is about this dish right now, not a permanent quality.

items.hr: Boa noite. Tem mesa para duas pessoas?
items.en: Good evening. Do you have a table for two?

items.hr: Queria a ementa, se faz favor.
items.en: I would like the menu, please.
items.note: ementa is the usual word in Portugal

items.en: For me, the roast cod.
items.note: para mim marks your own choice

items.en: It is very good, thank you.
items.note: estar for how the food tastes today

items.hr: Queríamos pagar a conta, por favor.
items.en: We would like to pay the bill, please.
items.note: pagar a conta means to pay the bill

activities.title: At the table
activities.intro: Practise the fixed phrases of a restaurant visit.

questions.prompt: Which word is used in Portugal for the printed list of dishes?
questions.explanation: ementa is the standard European Portuguese word; cardápio is Brazilian usage.

questions.prompt: Which sentence asks the waiter for the bill?
questions.explanation: conta is the bill; troco is the change you get back after paying.

questions.answer: Queríamos pagar a conta, por favor.
questions.explanation: 'We would like to pay the bill, please.' is 'Queríamos pagar a conta, por favor.'

activities.title: Dinner at the restaurant
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A waiter serves you through a whole meal, so order, comment and pay using the phrases from this lesson.

days.title: At the market: quantities and weights
days.objective: Buy food by weight, unit and container using the correct quantity expressions.
days.paretoFocus: Every food purchase needs a quantity word, and the pattern quantity plus de plus product covers all of them at once.
drills: Ask for five different foods, each with a different quantity word.
Say the same shopping list again halving every quantity.
Name three containers and the product that normally comes in each.

items: Which little word joins the quantity to the product?
How many units are in uma dúzia?
Give three container words you would use at a food shop.

activities.title: Quantidades e pesos
activities.intro: Portuguese joins a quantity to a product with de: um quilo de arroz, uma garrafa de água. Weights use quilo and grama, and everyday amounts use meio, dúzia, pacote, lata and garrafa. No article goes before the product after de.

items.hr: Um quilo de batatas, se faz favor.
items.en: A kilo of potatoes, please.
items.note: de links the quantity to the product

items.en: Half a kilo of ripe tomatoes.
items.note: meio quilo is 500 grams

items.hr: Duzentos e cinquenta gramas de queijo.
items.en: Two hundred and fifty grams of cheese.
A dozen fresh eggs.
items.note: uma dúzia is twelve

items.hr: Levo um pacote de arroz e uma garrafa de azeite.
items.en: I will take a packet of rice and a bottle of olive oil.

activities.title: Comprar a peso
activities.intro: Practise quantity words, weights and the linking preposition.

questions.prompt: How many items does uma dúzia contain?
questions.explanation: uma dúzia is twelve, and meia dúzia is six.

questions.prompt: Which word joins a quantity to the product being bought?

questions.explanation: 'A dozen fresh eggs.' is 'Uma dúzia de ovos frescos.'

activities.title: At the fruit stall

days.title: The body and how I feel
days.objective: Name the main parts of the body and say what hurts or how you feel.
days.paretoFocus: Saying where it hurts is essential in a pharmacy or clinic, and the verb doer works backwards compared with English.
drills: Point at eight parts of your body and name each one out loud.
Say five sentences about aches, switching between the singular and plural forms of the verb.
Practise three ways of saying you feel unwell without naming a body part.

items: Whose form does the verb doer agree with, the person or the body part?
What does the word constipado mean in Portugal?
Give the eu form of sentir-se in a negative sentence.

activities.title: What hurts?
activities.intro: The verb doer agrees with the body part, not with the person: dói-me a cabeça means literally the head hurts to me. If the body part is plural, the verb becomes doem. Another common pattern is ter dores de plus the body part.

items.en: I have had a headache since yesterday.
items.note: the verb agrees with a cabeça, not with eu

items.en: My back hurts.
items.note: costas is plural in Portuguese, so doem

items.en: I have a sore throat.
items.note: ter dores de plus body part

items.en: I do not feel well today.
items.note: sentir-se, with the pronoun before the verb after não

items.en: I have a cold and a temperature.
items.note: constipado means having a cold in Portugal

activities.title: Dores e sintomas
activities.intro: Practise the verb doer and the vocabulary for feeling ill.

questions.prompt: What does the sentence 'Estou constipado.' mean in Portugal?
questions.explanation: constipado is a false friend: in Portugal it always refers to a common cold.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form for 'my feet hurt': '___ os pés.'
questions.explanation: os pés is plural so the verb is doem, and me shows the pain is yours.

questions.prompt: Fill in the two words that give the eu form of sentir-se after a negative: 'Não ___ ___ nada bem.'
questions.explanation: The negative não pulls the pronoun forward, so it is me sinto and not sinto-me.

questions.prompt: Fill in the plural noun for pain: 'Tenho ___ de dentes.'
questions.explanation: The fixed expression uses the plural: ter dores de dentes.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'I have a headache and I am tired.'
questions.explanation: The verb comes first with its pronoun attached, then the body part as subject.

questions.prompt: Listen closely and fill the gap: 'Dói-me a ___ desde ontem.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Dói-me a cabeça desde ontem.', which means 'I have had a headache since yesterday.'

questions.prompt: Type the Portuguese for: 'I have a cold and a temperature.'
questions.explanation: 'I have a cold and a temperature.' is 'Estou constipado e com febre.'

activities.title: At the pharmacy
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. You explain your symptoms to a pharmacist, using doer, ter dores and sentir-se.

lines.hr: Boa tarde. Como se sente?
lines.en: Good afternoon. How are you feeling?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Não me sinto bem. Dói-me muito a garganta.
lines.en: I do not feel well. My throat hurts a lot.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tem febre?
lines.en: Do you have a temperature?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tenho, e também me doem as costas.
lines.en: I do, and my back hurts as well.

lines.hr: Parece uma constipação forte.
lines.en: It sounds like a bad cold.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Obrigado. Espero sentir-me melhor amanhã.
lines.en: Thank you. I hope to feel better tomorrow.

days.title: Descrever pessoas: o aspeto e o feitio
days.objective: Describe what someone looks like and what they are like using ser, ter and usar.
days.paretoFocus: Describing a person is how you identify who you are meeting, who served you or who you are talking about, and it recycles adjective agreement.
drills: Describe three people you know in two sentences each.
List five appearance adjectives and five personality adjectives.
Describe yourself as if someone had to recognise you at a station.

items: Which verb do you use for hair and eyes, ser or ter?
Which verb do you use for glasses and beards?
Give two adjectives for appearance and two for personality.

activities.title: What is she like?
activities.intro: Use ser plus an adjective for general qualities such as height, build and character. Use ter for the features a person has, like hair and eyes, and usar for things they wear such as glasses or a beard. All adjectives still agree in gender and number.

items.hr: Ela é alta e tem cabelo castanho.
items.en: She is tall and has brown hair.
items.note: ser for build, ter for hair

items.hr: Ele é magro e usa óculos.
items.en: He is thin and wears glasses.
items.note: usar for glasses, beard, hats

items.hr: A minha avó tem olhos verdes.
items.en: My grandmother has green eyes.

items.hr: O Pedro é simpático e muito calmo.
items.en: Pedro is friendly and very calm.
items.note: o feitio means the personality

items.hr: Ela tem cerca de trinta anos.
items.en: She is about thirty.
items.note: cerca de means approximately

activities.title: Aspeto e feitio
activities.intro: Practise the verbs and adjectives used to describe people.

questions.prompt: Which pair describes physical appearance rather than personality?
questions.explanation: alto and magro are about the body; the other pairs describe character.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: 'Ela ___ cabelo curto.'
questions.explanation: Hair, eyes and other features a person has take the verb ter.

questions.prompt: Fill in the adjective meaning friendly, agreeing with a woman: 'A Marta é muito ___.'
questions.explanation: The adjective ends in -o for men and changes to -a for women.

questions.prompt: Fill in the verb used for wearing glasses, in the ele form: 'O meu pai ___ óculos há anos.'
questions.explanation: usar covers glasses, hats and beards, where English says wears or has.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'My brother is tall and has blue eyes.'
questions.explanation: ser carries the build and ter carries the eyes, with azuis agreeing in the plural.

questions.prompt: Type the word you hear: 'Ela é alta e tem cabelo ___.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Ela é alta e tem cabelo castanho.', which means 'She is tall and has brown hair.'
questions.audioText: Ela é alta e tem cabelo castanho.

questions.prompt: Write it in Portuguese: 'She is about thirty.'
questions.answer: Ela tem cerca de trinta anos.
questions.explanation: 'She is about thirty.' is 'Ela tem cerca de trinta anos.'

activities.title: Who is picking me up?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Someone is meeting you at the station and you exchange descriptions, so describe appearance and character.

lines.hr: Como é que eu o reconheço na estação?
lines.en: How will I recognise you at the station?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Assim já não me perco. Até logo!
lines.en: Then I will not get lost. See you later!

days.title: Animals and nature
days.objective: Talk about pets, farm animals and the natural landscape around you.
days.paretoFocus: Animals and nature words come up constantly in small talk about pets, walks and weekends away, and they drill the tricky -al to -ais plural.
drills: Name six animals out loud and say whether each lives at home, on a farm or in the wild.
Describe a park or beach you know in three sentences.
Make three plurals of nouns ending in -l and say them aloud.

items: How do you form the plural of a noun ending in -al?
Give the words for dog, cat, cow and sheep.
Which verb do you use to say there are many trees somewhere?

activities.title: Animais e paisagem
activities.intro: Nouns ending in -al form their plural in -ais, so animal becomes animais. Use há to say there is or there are, without changing for singular or plural. Nature words like campo, serra and beira-mar describe where you spend free time.

items.hr: Tenho um cão e dois gatos em casa.
items.en: I have a dog and two cats at home.
There are many trees in this park.
items.note: há is the same for singular and plural

items.hr: No campo vemos vacas e ovelhas.
items.en: In the countryside we see cows and sheep.

items.hr: Gosto de passear à beira-mar ao domingo.
items.en: I like walking by the sea on Sundays.
items.note: à beira-mar means at the seaside

items.hr: Os pássaros cantam muito cedo de manhã.
items.en: The birds sing very early in the morning.

activities.title: Bichos e paisagens
activities.intro: Practise animal vocabulary, nature words and the -ais plural.

questions.prompt: What animal is an ovelha?
questions.explanation: ovelha is a sheep; a cow is vaca, a goat is cabra and a horse is cavalo.

questions.prompt: What is the plural of um animal?
questions.explanation: Nouns ending in -al drop the -l and take -is in the plural.

questions.prompt: Fill in the word for the sea: 'Passámos o dia à beira do ___.'
questions.explanation: o mar is the sea, and à beira do mar means at the seaside.

questions.prompt: Fill in the plural of árvore: 'O jardim tem muitas ___.'
questions.explanation: Nouns ending in -e simply add -s, keeping the written accent.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'There are many birds in this garden.'
questions.explanation: Há never changes, and em plus este contracts to neste.

questions.prompt: Listen and complete the sentence: 'Tenho um cão e dois ___ em casa.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Tenho um cão e dois gatos em casa.', which means 'I have a dog and two cats at home.'
questions.audioText: Tenho um cão e dois gatos em casa.

questions.prompt: Say it in Portuguese, in writing: 'The birds sing very early in the morning.'
questions.answer: Os pássaros cantam muito cedo de manhã.
questions.explanation: 'The birds sing very early in the morning.' is 'Os pássaros cantam muito cedo de manhã.'

activities.title: A walk in the countryside
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend asks about your pets and a walk in the countryside, so use animal and nature vocabulary.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tens animais em casa?
lines.en: Do you have pets at home?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tenho um cão pequeno e um gato preto.
lines.en: I have a small dog and a black cat.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E levas o cão a passear?
lines.en: And do you take the dog for walks?

lines.speaker: Me

days.title: Convidar, aceitar e recusar
days.objective: Invite someone to do something and accept or turn down an invitation politely.
days.paretoFocus: Social life runs on invitations, and a refusal without the right formula sounds cold, so the fixed replies matter as much as the invitation itself.
drills: Invite someone to three different activities using two different opening formulas.
Practise two enthusiastic acceptances and two polite refusals with a reason.
Refuse an invitation and then propose another moment instead.

items: What does the verb apetecer add to an invitation?
Give one short enthusiastic way of accepting.
How do you soften a refusal so it does not sound rude?

activities.title: Shall we arrange something?
activities.intro: Invitations often start with apetecer, which works like doer: apetece-te means it appeals to you. A refusal in Portuguese almost always includes thanks plus a reason, and often a promise to do it another time.

items.hr: Apetece-te ir ao cinema logo à noite?
items.en: Do you feel like going to the cinema tonight?
items.note: apetecer agrees with the activity, not the person

items.hr: Queres vir jantar lá a casa no sábado?
items.en: Do you want to come for dinner at my place on Saturday?
Of course, with great pleasure!
items.note: a warm, standard acceptance

items.en: Thank you, but I cannot today.
items.note: thanks plus a reason softens a refusal

items.hr: Fica para a próxima, está bem?
items.en: Let us leave it for next time, all right?
items.note: used to postpone rather than simply refuse

activities.title: Accepting or declining
activities.intro: Practise the formulas for inviting, accepting and refusing.

questions.prompt: Which reply accepts an invitation?
questions.explanation: The other three all postpone or decline the invitation.

questions.prompt: What is the question 'Apetece-te?' actually asking?
questions.explanation: apetecer expresses appetite or inclination for doing something.

questions.prompt: Fill in the verb form that completes this polite refusal: 'Obrigada, mas hoje não ___.'
questions.explanation: The eu form of poder is used to say you are unable to accept.

questions.prompt: Fill in the infinitive meaning to come: 'Queres ___ connosco ao concerto?'
questions.explanation: After querer the second verb stays in the infinitive, and vir means to come.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'Do you feel like going to the beach on Saturday?'
questions.explanation: The pronoun te attaches to apetece, and a plus a praia contracts to à praia.

questions.prompt: Listen, then type the missing word: 'Apetece-te ir ao ___ logo à noite?'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Apetece-te ir ao cinema logo à noite?', which means 'Do you feel like going to the cinema tonight?'
questions.audioText: Apetece-te ir ao cinema logo à noite?

questions.prompt: Put this into Portuguese: 'Let us leave it for next time, all right?'
questions.answer: Fica para a próxima, está bem?
questions.explanation: 'Let us leave it for next time, all right?' is 'Fica para a próxima, está bem?'

activities.title: An invitation for Saturday
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend invites you out twice, so refuse politely once and then accept a new proposal.

lines.hr: Apetece-te ir ao teatro na sexta-feira?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Obrigado, mas na sexta não posso. Trabalho até tarde.

lines.en: Agreed. We will meet at four at the entrance.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Até sábado então. Obrigado pelo convite!
lines.en: See you on Saturday then. Thanks for the invitation!

days.title: Useful irregular verbs: ir, vir, ver, dar
days.objective: Use the present tense of ir, vir, ver and dar correctly in everyday sentences.
days.paretoFocus: These four verbs are among the most frequent in spoken Portuguese and they are all irregular, so learning them as blocks unlocks a lot of ordinary speech.
drills: Say all five present forms of each of the four verbs out loud, twice.
Write four sentences, one with each verb, about your own week.
Say three fixed expressions built on dar and use them in a sentence.

items: Give the eu form of each of the four verbs.
What is the difference in direction between ir and vir?
What does the expression dar um passeio mean?

activities.title: Vou, venho, vejo, dou
activities.intro: ir means to go away from here, while vir means to come towards the speaker. ver and dar are short verbs with irregular eu forms. Portuguese also uses dar in many fixed expressions, such as dar um passeio and dar os parabéns.

items.en: I am going to the supermarket now.
items.note: ir: vou, vais, vai, vamos, vão

items.hr: Ela vem de comboio às seis.
items.en: She is coming by train at six.
items.note: vir: venho, vens, vem, vimos, vêm

items.hr: Vejo o mar da minha janela.

activities.title: Four irregular verbs
activities.intro: Practise the present forms of dar, ver, vir and ir.

questions.prompt: Which of these is the eu form of the verb vir?
questions.explanation: vir has an irregular eu form with an added nh: venho.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: 'Eles ___ um presente à professora.'
questions.explanation: The eles form of dar is dão, with a nasal ending.

questions.prompt: Fill in the eu form of the verb ver: '___ televisão todas as noites.'
questions.explanation: ver changes its stem in the first person, giving vejo.

questions.prompt: Fill in the nós form of the verb ir: '___ ao teatro esta noite.'
questions.explanation: The nós form of ir is vamos, which also serves as let us go.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'They are coming here tomorrow morning.'
questions.explanation: vêm is the eles form of vir and carries a circumflex to separate it from vem.

questions.prompt: Listen and fill in the word you hear: 'Vou ao ___ agora.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Vou ao supermercado agora.', which means 'I am going to the supermarket now.'

questions.prompt: Type the Portuguese for: 'After dinner we go for a walk.'
questions.answer: Depois do jantar damos um passeio.
questions.explanation: 'After dinner we go for a walk.' is 'Depois do jantar damos um passeio.'

activities.title: Plans with four verbs
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. You and a friend arrange an evening out, and all four of today's verbs come up along the way.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vais à cidade hoje à tarde?
lines.en: Are you going into town this afternoon?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vou. Queres vir comigo?
lines.en: I am. Do you want to come with me?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vou sim. Podemos ver a exposição nova.
lines.en: Yes I will. We can see the new exhibition.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Boa ideia. Depois damos um passeio junto ao rio.
lines.en: Good idea. Afterwards we will take a walk by the river.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: A que horas vens buscar-me?
lines.en: What time are you coming to pick me up?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vou de autocarro e chego às quatro.
lines.en: I am going by bus and I will arrive at four.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vejo-te à porta, então.
lines.en: I will see you at the door, then.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Combinado. Dou-te um toque quando chegar.
lines.en: Agreed. I will give you a ring when I arrive.

days.title: A1 review II
days.objective: Consolidate the last eight days (transport, formality, demonstratives, plurals, jobs, hobbies, plans and phone calls) and put it all to work at the market.
days.paretoFocus: Review beats new material: re-activating these eight themes now locks them in. The market dialogue recombines demonstratives, plurals and polite register in one real scene.
drills: Speed round: say one sentence from each of the last 8 days.
Role-play the market dialogue aloud from the 'Me' side only.
Review this week's word list in the Words tab.

items: Recall: apanhar vs perder o autocarro.
Switch one question between tu and o senhor register.
Pluralise pão, limão and mão from memory.

activities.title: Oito dias num relance
activities.intro: One anchor per theme. If any line feels shaky, revisit that day before the checkpoint.

items.hr: Apanho o autocarro na paragem. / Perdi o comboio!
items.en: transport: catch the bus at the stop / I missed the train!
register: the verb ending switches the formality

items.hr: Isto é meu, isso é teu.
items.en: This is mine, that is yours.
items.note: The demonstrative triangle: isto in my space, isso in yours, aquilo far from both.

items.hr: Comprei dois pães e três limões.
items.en: I bought two loaves and three lemons.
items.note: The three -ão plurals, one example each: pão and pães, limão and limões, mão and mãos.

items.hr: Sou enfermeira e trabalho num hospital.
items.en: I am a nurse and I work in a hospital.
items.note: Professions take no article after ser, and workplaces take num or numa.

items.hr: Jogo à bola e toco guitarra ao fim de semana.
items.en: hobbies: jogar for sports, tocar for instruments
making plans: invitation, flexible yes, sealed deal
Hello? Would you like to leave a message?
items.note: On the phone: ligar to call, atender to pick up, deixar recado to leave a message.

activities.title: Everything mixed together
activities.intro: Mixed questions from lessons 1-8 of this block.

questions.prompt: The European Portuguese word for 'tram' is…
questions.explanation: O elétrico = the tram; o comboio = the train.

questions.prompt: Formal version of 'Tens troco?' (Do you have change?) to a shopkeeper:
questions.explanation: Formal register: o senhor + 3rd person verb; 'você' is grammatically formal but often sounds blunt said to someone's face.

questions.prompt: The plural of 'pão' is…
questions.explanation: pão → pães, like cão → cães. 'Panes' is the Spanish plural, not Portuguese.

questions.prompt: 'Apetece-me um café' means…
options: I want to buy a coffee
questions.explanation: apetecer + me = it appeals to me = I feel like.

questions.prompt: Ask about the thing in your friend's hand: '___ é isso?' (What)
questions.explanation: O que é isso…? isso because it is in YOUR listener's hand.

questions.prompt: Complete (profession, feminine, no article): 'O meu pai é médico e a minha mãe é ___.' (teacher)
questions.explanation: Ela é professora, no article before professions.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Vou apanhar o ___ para a Baixa.' (the bus)
questions.explanation: apanhar o autocarro, the pt-PT word for bus, always.

questions.prompt: Put in order: offer a choice between a message with you or a text.
questions.explanation: Queres deixar recado ou mandas uma mensagem? two phone options, tu register.

questions.prompt: Play the audio and complete: 'Apanho o ___ na paragem. / Perdi o comboio!'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Apanho o autocarro na paragem. / Perdi o comboio!', which means 'transport: catch the bus at the stop / I missed the train!'

activities.title: At the market
activities.intro: Shopping at the market, demonstratives, plurals and polite register all working together. Read both parts aloud.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Bom dia! Diga, faz favor.
lines.en: Good morning! What can I get you?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Bom dia. Quanto custam estas laranjas?
lines.en: Good morning. How much are these oranges?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Essas custam um euro e vinte o quilo.
lines.en: Those cost one euro twenty a kilo.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Então queria dois quilos, e também aqueles limões ali.
lines.en: Then I'd like two kilos, and also those lemons over there.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Com certeza. Mais alguma coisa?
lines.en: Certainly. Anything else?

lines.speaker: Me

lines.hr: Aqui tem. São quatro euros e cinquenta.
